encounters.cc: Progressive muscle weakness, inability to sit unsupported, and feeding deterioration

lines: Progressive muscle weakness, inability to sit unsupported, and feeding deterioration
This 1-year-old male with history of congenital aganglionic megacolon, glycogen storage disease, and mucolipidosis returns to neurology clinic for follow-up evaluation.
He has been followed by multiple specialties since birth, with recent genetics evaluation six months ago.
His parents report that he has not been able to sit without support, and over the past 2 months he has developed increasing irritability and difficulty swallowing.
They note that he tires easily during bottle feeding and often stops before finishing.
Over the past week, he has had several episodes of vomiting and rapid breathing.
His growth has been poor; he is below the 5th percentile for both weight and length.
Developmental history reveals that he smiled at 2 months but has not been able to roll over or push up with his arms.
- von Gierke disease (Glycogen Storage Disease Type I) (diagnosed 2020-07-15)
- Global developmental delay with axial hypotonia
